title: Knight Probability in Chessboard
summary: Given an n x n chessboard, a knight starts at a specific cell (row, column) and makes exactly k moves.
statement: Given an n x n chessboard, a knight starts at a specific cell (row, column) and makes exactly k moves. Each move consists of two cells in a cardinal direction followed by one cell in an orthogonal direction. At each move, the knight selects one of the eight possible moves uniformly at random. The knight continues moving until it has made k moves or it moves off the chessboard. Return the probability that the knight remains on the board after making k moves.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 25; 0 <= k <= 100; the starting square is on the board.
Each of eight knight moves is equally likely; return the probability the knight remains on-board after k moves.
hints: Probability mass that moves off-board disappears.
Propagate each square’s mass equally to its valid knight destinations for k rounds.
For every state, add probability/8 to each in-bounds destination; sum after k rounds.
Every length-k move sequence has probability 8^-k, and dynamic programming merges sequences ending on the same square.
editorial: Every length-k move sequence has probability 8^-k, and dynamic programming merges sequences ending on the same square.

tests.explanation: Exactly four of the 64 two-move sequences remain on the board, giving 0.0625.
With zero moves, the knight remains on its starting square with probability one.
